target_customer: Enterprises, regulated industries (such as finance) and scientific users that need AI models whose outputs can be audited and traced; no named customers yet
problem: Large language models are opaque; users cannot trace an output to training data or internal concepts, which blocks debugging, auditing and trust.
business_model: Interpretable foundation models, open-sourced base model (Apache 2.0) with a platform called Clarity and planned API and agent access (pricing not found)

founders.name: Julius Adebayo
founders.background_notes: Co-authored a widely cited 2018 paper on the unreliability of saliency methods for understanding deep models (per TechCrunch).

founders.name: Aya Abdelsalam Ismail
founders.background_notes: Co-founder per TechCrunch; no further background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building an inherently interpretable LLM with a concept layer that traces each token to training data and concepts is research-grade; it needs extra data annotation and had to match the capability of ordinary models (the company claims about 90% at 8B parameters, per TechCrunch).

defensibility.rationale: A novel architecture and published research give a head start, but the model is open-sourced under Apache 2.0, so defensibility rests on speed, the annotated data and the platform rather than secrecy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing an incumbent copying or buying the approach as of the sources read (Feb 2026).

market_need_then: Regulated sectors and enterprises were asking for explainability and audit trails for LLMs; the company cites finance and science as uses, but no customer demand figures or named customers were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses guidelabs.ai rather than an exact .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and research-led; blog posts titled around interpretability scaling laws and papers.

branding.brand_signature: Steerling-8B, the first inherently interpretable model released openly
branding.community_and_virality: Open-source release got coverage from TechCrunch, Dataconomy and international tech blogs in February 2026; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic descriptive name; recognition comes from the Steerling-8B release and research papers rather than from the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Guide Labs, a Winter 2024 YC company, raised a $9.3M seed led by Initialized in November 2024 and in February 2026 open-sourced Steerling-8B, an 8B-parameter model that traces every output token to training data and concepts. It is still early: no named customers, no later round found, and no exit, so the outcome is open; its strengths are the founders' interpretability research and a research-grade technical lead, while the open license and well-funded frontier labs and interpretability rivals are the main risks.
notes: Seed: company blog (2024-11-17) says $9.3M led by Initialized; TechCrunch says $9M; Pulse 2.0 and Seedtable agree on about $9M and November 2024 (Pulse 2.0 article is dated December 2025). One job site shows $130K, which conflicts and is ignored. Founding year 2023 per YC listing as relayed by search; another source says 2024. Founders' prior employers and education beyond MIT PhD not found. Competition: no dated sources near the Winter 2024 batch found; the interpretability startup Goodfire announced a seed only in August 2024, after the batch, so competitor list is empty. Name origin not found. The company site mentions a product called Clarity. Web Archive skipped.
